---
title: "How Much Memory Does Llama-3 70B Actually Need?"
description: "A 3-minute calculation with mlsysim that answers the question every ML engineer asks."
date: 2026-04-01
categories: [serving, memory, llm]
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import mlsysim
from mlsysim.physics import calc_kv_cache_size
from mlsysim.solvers import ServingModel

llama70b = mlsysim.Models.Language.Llama3_70B
h100 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H100
a100 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.A100

_params_b = llama70b.parameters.to("dimensionless").magnitude / 1e9
_fp16_size = llama70b.size_in_bytes()
_int8_size = llama70b.size_in_bytes(mlsysim.ureg("1 byte"))
_int4_size = llama70b.size_in_bytes(mlsysim.ureg("0.5 byte"))

_fp16_gb = _fp16_size.to("GB").magnitude
_int8_gb = _int8_size.to("GB").magnitude
_int4_gb = _int4_size.to("GB").magnitude

_h100_gib = h100.memory.capacity.to("GiB").magnitude
_h100_gb = h100.memory.capacity.to("GB").magnitude
_a100_gib = a100.memory.capacity.to("GiB").magnitude

_layers = llama70b.layers
_heads = llama70b.heads
_kv_heads = llama70b.kv_heads
_head_dim = llama70b.hidden_dim // llama70b.heads
_gqa_ratio = _heads // _kv_heads

_kv_4k = calc_kv_cache_size(
    n_layers=_layers,
    n_heads=_kv_heads,
    head_dim=_head_dim,
    seq_len=4096,
    batch_size=1,
    bytes_per_elem=2,
)
_kv_32k = calc_kv_cache_size(
    n_layers=_layers,
    n_heads=_kv_heads,
    head_dim=_head_dim,
    seq_len=32768,
    batch_size=1,
    bytes_per_elem=2,
)
_kv_4k_gb = _kv_4k.to("GB").magnitude
_kv_4k_mb = _kv_4k.to("MB").magnitude
_kv_32k_gb = _kv_32k.to("GB").magnitude

_rem_int4 = h100.memory.capacity - _int4_size
_rem_int4_gb = _rem_int4.to("GB").magnitude
_rem_int4_mb = _rem_int4.to("MB").magnitude
_max_req_4k = int(_rem_int4.to("byte").magnitude // _kv_4k.to("byte").magnitude)
_max_req_32k = int(_rem_int4.to("byte").magnitude // _kv_32k.to("byte").magnitude)
```

Every ML engineer eventually confronts the same capacity problem: whether `{python} llama70b.name` (`{python} f"{_params_b:.1f}B"` parameters) fits on the available hardware.

The answer depends on three quantities: **precision**, **KV cache**, and **batch size**.
The calculation takes 30 seconds.

## The Weights

```{python}
#| echo: true
import mlsysim

llama70b = mlsysim.Models.Language.Llama3_70B

# FP16: 2 bytes per parameter
fp16_size = llama70b.size_in_bytes()
print(f"FP16 weights: {fp16_size.to('GB'):~.1f}")

# INT8: 1 byte per parameter
int8_size = llama70b.size_in_bytes(mlsysim.ureg("1 byte"))
print(f"INT8 weights: {int8_size.to('GB'):~.1f}")

# INT4: 0.5 bytes per parameter
int4_size = llama70b.size_in_bytes(mlsysim.ureg("0.5 byte"))
print(f"INT4 weights: {int4_size.to('GB'):~.1f}")
```

**Result:** `{python} f"{_fp16_gb:.1f} GB"` in FP16, `{python} f"{_int8_gb:.1f} GB"` in INT8, and `{python} f"{_int4_gb:.1f} GB"` in INT4.

An H100 or A100 has `{python} f"{_h100_gib:.0f} GiB"` (`{python} f"{_h100_gb:.1f} GB"`), so `{python} llama70b.name` in FP16 **does not fit on one GPU**.
Serving it requires either tensor parallelism ($\text{TP}=2$) or quantization to INT8/INT4.

## The KV Cache (The Hidden Memory Consumer)

Weights are only part of the total. Each active request also needs a KV cache:

```{python}
#| echo: true
from mlsysim.physics import calc_kv_cache_size

head_dim = llama70b.hidden_dim // llama70b.heads
kv_per_request = calc_kv_cache_size(
    n_layers=llama70b.layers,
    n_heads=llama70b.kv_heads,
    head_dim=head_dim,
    seq_len=4096,
    batch_size=1,
    bytes_per_elem=2,
)
print(f"KV cache per request (4K context): {kv_per_request.to('GB'):~.2f} ({kv_per_request.to('MB'):~.0f})")
```

At `{python} f"{_kv_4k_gb:.2f} GB"` (`{python} f"{_kv_4k_mb:,.0f} MB"`) per request across `{python} f"{_layers}"` layers and `{python} f"{_kv_heads}"` GQA KV heads (`{python} f"{_head_dim}"`-dim per head), an `{python} f"{_h100_gib:.0f} GiB"` (`{python} f"{_h100_gb:.1f} GB"`) H100 serving INT4 `{python} llama70b.name` has:

- `{python} f"{_int4_gb:.1f} GB"` for weights
- `{python} f"{_rem_int4_gb:.1f} GB"` (`{python} f"{_rem_int4_mb:,.0f} MB"`) remaining for KV cache
- **`{python} f"{_rem_int4_gb:.1f} GB"` / `{python} f"{_kv_4k_gb:.2f} GB"` $\approx$ `{python} f"{_max_req_4k}"` concurrent requests max**

At 32K context, the KV cache grows to `{python} f"{_kv_32k_gb:.2f} GB"` per request, which leaves room for at most **`{python} f"{_max_req_32k}"` concurrent requests**.

## The Full Picture

```{python}
#| echo: true
from mlsysim.solvers import ServingModel

result = ServingModel().solve(
    model=mlsysim.Models.Language.Llama3_70B,
    hardware=mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H100,
    seq_len=4096,
    batch_size=1,
    precision="fp16",
)
print(f"Feasible:    {result.feasible}")
print(f"Memory util: {result.memory_utilization:.1%}")
```

**The conclusion:** A `{python} f"{_params_b:.1f}B"`-parameter model needs more than `{python} f"{_fp16_gb:.1f} GB"`. It needs
`{python} f"{_fp16_gb:.1f} GB"` + ($\text{KV cache} \times \text{concurrent requests}$). At production batch sizes and long contexts,
the KV cache can consume *more* memory than the weights.

## What To Do About It

| Strategy | Memory Impact | Trade-off |
|:---------|:--------------|:----------|
| INT4 quantization | $4\times$ smaller weights (`{python} f"{_fp16_gb:.1f} GB"` $\to$ `{python} f"{_int4_gb:.1f} GB"`) | ~2--5% accuracy loss |
| GQA (built into Llama-3) | $`{python} f"{_gqa_ratio}"`\times$ smaller KV cache (`{python} f"{_heads}"` $\to$ `{python} f"{_kv_heads}"` KV heads) | None (architectural) |
| KV cache INT8 | $2\times$ smaller KV cache (`{python} f"{_kv_4k_gb:.2f} GB"` $\to$ `{python} f"{_kv_4k_gb / 2:.2f} GB"` at 4K) | Negligible quality loss |
| Tensor parallelism ($\text{TP}=2$) | Split across 2 GPUs (`{python} f"{_fp16_gb / 2:.1f} GB"` weights/GPU) | Adds NVLink communication |
| PagedAttention (vLLM) | Eliminates KV fragmentation | ~20--40% more concurrent requests |

## Reproducing the Calculation

```bash
pip install mlsysim
mlsysim serve Llama3_70B H100 --seq-len 4096 --batch-size 1
```
